land.text: the Greek state taken over by the colonels' coup of 21 April 1967

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom row ends 1966 and the junta row starts 1967; the monarchy itself lasted formally to 1 June 1973.

land.text: the whole Greek state after the regime fell on 24 July 1974

successors.note: Cliopatria's junta row runs to 1975 and the Third Hellenic Republic row starts 1976, leaving no row for 1975's republic; the successor starts 24 July 1974 here.

keyframe_review.note: 122,017 km2 for 1967-72 against the infobox 131,957 km2: ratio 0.92, within a factor of two (the Cliopatria outline loses some island area). The page names no territorial change in the dictatorship, so the outline stands.

correction.text: shape unchanged; the years change: the regime fell on 24 July 1974, so the shape holds for 1973-1974 only and 1975 belongs to the Third Hellenic Republic

keyframe_review.note: 123,711 km2 against 131,957 km2 (ratio 0.94). Cliopatria runs this row to 1975, but 'Ioannidis ruled until it fell on 24 July 1974'. Years only: the outline is the same land.

region.text: the Greek state under the colonels, capital Athens

ledger.note: 1967: a group of right-wing army officers seizes power on 21 April. Infobox 'Coup d'etat of 21 April: 21 April 1967'; the text names Pattakos, Papadopoulos and Makarezos. Status 'Unitary constitutional monarchy under a military dictatorship (1967-1973)'. The page gives the capital Athens; the land (all of Greece) is the reading of the state's name.

1973: Papadopoulos 'abolished the monarchy and declared Greece a republic' on 1 June (infobox 'Republic declared: 1 June 1973'; the 29 July 1973 referendum was 'not recognised by the political parties'). On 25 November 1973 Ioannidis overthrew Papadopoulos in a counter-coup. The land is unchanged.

1974: the junta falls on 24 July. 'Ioannidis ruled until it fell on 24 July 1974' under 'the pressure of the Turkish invasion of Cyprus'; the fall 'led to the Metapolitefsi ... and the establishment of the Third Hellenic Republic' (Greek junta page); the Metapolitefsi page has Karamanlis sworn in as Prime Minister at 4 a.m. on 24 July 1974.

wars.name: Turkish invasion of Cyprus

zones.text: the north of Cyprus taken by Turkey in July-August 1974, 'approximately 36% of the island'

wars.outcome: The junta-backed National Guard coup of 15 July 1974 against Makarios led to the Turkish landing of 20 July; 'On 23 July 1974 the Greek military junta collapsed mainly because of the events in Cyprus' and Karamanlis was sworn in as Prime Minister on 24 July. No Greek territory changed hands; the north of Cyprus went to Turkey and the Turkish Cypriots.
wars.note: No Greek border moved; the zone is the Cypriot ground that changed hands (reviewer eu-22-d, from the Turkish invasion page), as in the Republic of Cyprus and turkish-republic-of-northern-cyprus dossiers. The Turkish invasion page dates the collapse 23 July, the Greek junta page 24 July, the Metapolitefsi page has Gizikis's meeting on 23 July and Karamanlis sworn in on 24 July; the dossier uses 24 July.

certainty.note: Greece's land frontiers were treaty lines before the coup; the pages opened record no change in 1967-74. The Aegean sea limits are not land.

notes: Cliopatria rows: 'Greek junta' 1967..1975 (2 shapes, 122,017 and 123,711 km2). The regime ended on 24 July 1974, so the 1973 shape is marked adjust for its years only; 1975 is the Third Hellenic Republic (own dossier), and Cliopatria has no row for the republic until 1976. Rulers not written: the Greek junta page's infobox lists only Papadopoulos (1973) and Gizikis (1973-74) with Ioannidis as the unlisted strongman and Zoitakis as regent to 1972, which is not a full list. Pages silent on the Dodecanese and the Aegean (no change recorded 1967-74). Needs from other groups: kingdom-of-greece (exists, eu-22-a) and the Republic of Cyprus dossier carry the Cyprus side. Page budget 1-2 pages: the Greek junta page plus the Turkish invasion page (also cited by the Cyprus dossiers); the Metapolitefsi page is cited in the third-hellenic-republic dossier.
